summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (115/294)

data.turoyo: Mə ksoyəm? Komiḥayər b ruḥe, aydarbo kobəʕ, d tole i nuqṭaṯe du admo?
data.translation: Er weiß nicht, was er tun soll, wie er den Blutstropfen entfernen soll.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (53/135)

data.turoyo: Huwe kdoʕər li konayḏe si ḥoṯo, mḥayarre u babo w u nuxroyo di ḥoṯo.
data.translation: Er kehrt in sein Zelt zurück, zu der Schwester. Der Vater und der Freier der Schwester sind aufs äußerste bestürzt.

rationale: First full contextual example for active Preterit mḥayarre; inherited item gives only the bare form and a proposed alternative. Retain the form provisionally.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (115/134)

data.turoyo: Mḥayro ġalabe, hnela, qrela li xodumtayḏa, mʕayaṭla aʕla, əmmo: "Man ʕabər l riši larke b lalyo?"
data.translation: Sie war höchlichst erstaunt. Sie rief ihre Dienerin, schalt sie aus und sprach: Wer ist heute Nacht hier zu mir hereingekommen?

rationale: Thin Infectum cell following the inherited provisional filing at 41/15; the alternative Detransitive analysis is explicitly retained as a question.

data.translation: Die Besitzer der Ziegen, die Hirten, ja alle Dorfbewohner waren ratlos.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (48/12)

data.translation: Der Mann wußte nicht, was er sagen sollte. Wie soll er denn essen? Und Holz gibt es dort nicht; wie soll er welches aufladen?

rationale: Thin Detransitive Preterit cell; masculine unprefixed state and following practical questions. Placement provisional like inherited mḥayarno.

data.translation: Jetzt hat er von mir etwas verlangt, das süßer ist als alles, was es auf Erden gibt. Und ich bin ratlos und weiß nicht, was ich machen soll."

summary: Retain stem II of ḥyr 2 and distinguish it from visual ḥyr 1. All 18 records express confusion, perplexity or being at a loss; different edition paraphrases do not establish separate senses.

Experiencers are subjects. Causes/problems are supplied by m- or ʕal- in inherited examples, by context or following questions in these texts; b ruḥe at 115/294 locates the personal state and is not automatically the reflection idiom of ḥyr 1.

Detransitive forms are experiential states without an expressed agent. luF 3/69 supplies plural mḥayri; 115/294 supplies overt prefixed ko-miḥayər. They do not by themselves resolve all unprefixed active/Detransitive ambiguities.
Part. Pass. is clearest after fyš: fayišina mḥayre, fayəšno mḥayro, fayšowayno mḥayarto. Different person/time marking belongs to fyš; the state form is kept in Part. Pass.
The inherited Infectum cell has one textual example, not two: its Russian analysis is the note field of the 41/15 example. No duplicate-example correction is warranted.

Hors 2/103 is already the MM 103 quotation; PrS 44/34 is already the prs 126/11 quotation. Keep inherited citations and avoid duplicate text. The additional 64/223 reference has a different, shorter realization and is queried.
mḥayro is the state complement of fayəšno; first-person and temporal marking belongs to fyš. The token supports round-1 Detransitive Part. Pass. sense 1, not active Preterit or a new box.

The Detransitive Part. Pass. cell already has five examples after round 1, including fayəšno mḥayro with an explicit problem clause at 51/57. The Jan context is valid but adds no gap or clearly better contrast, so it is recorded as support without another example.
The later mdamro belongs to a different root and is not counted as a second occurrence of ḥyr 2. No looking/reflection meaning of homonym ḥyr 1 is inferred.
All 1 supplied occurrences were checked in input order, including repeated forms within one verse. Jan English is project machine translation; it is not independent semantic evidence.

Can unprefixed mḥayro/mḥayər in 41/15,44/47,48/12,52/17,73/422,115/134,136 be distinguished as active Infectum versus Detransitive Preterit? The entry itself leaves this open; new placements remain provisional.
53/135 mḥayarre: confirm active Preterit agent segmentation versus a Detransitive reading and the inherited suggested alternative mḥairi; no source form is silently replaced.

Does the 64/223 reference on the inherited Part. Pass. example cite a variant rather than its exact wording? Source 64/223 reads Lə gḏaʕ, mə soyəm, faš mḥayro, while the quoted text matches PrS 44/34.
Confirm feminine Part. Pass. mḥayarto at 63/263 alongside invariant-looking mḥayro in other predicates.
Clarify whether 64/223 is an additional form parallel
rationale: The supplied 64/223 is “Lə gḏaʕ, mə soyəm, faš mḥayro” (he did not know what to do and was at a loss), not the quoted search-and-return-home sentence. That complete sentence is supplied under PrS 44/34, while the entry already cites prs 126/11. Since 64/223 does attest mḥayro and may intentionally be a form parallel, do not mechanically replace it with the automatic best match. Clarify the status of this secondary reference.
